title: Cedric Jones: Oklahoma's Career Sack Leader, 1992-1995
question: Who is Oklahoma's all-time career sack leader?
answer: Cedric Jones, a defensive end from Houston who played at Oklahoma from 1992 to 1995, finished with 31.5 career sacks, the top mark in the school's record book supplement published in 2019. The Giants made him the fifth overall pick in the 1996 NFL Draft.
summary: Cedric Jones played at Oklahoma from 1992 to 1995 and holds the career sack record with 31.5, plus a five-sack game against Texas Tech in 1994.
body: Cedric Jones came to Norman from Lamar High School in Houston and played four seasons at Oklahoma, 1992 through 1995. He spent three of them under Gary Gibbs and the last under Howard Schnellenberger, and he left as the most productive pass rusher the program had recorded.

The numbers in the Sooners' own record book supplement, published in 2019, still carry his name. His 31.5 career sacks from 1992 to 1995 lead the school. His 14.0 sacks in 1994 are the best single season, a mark he shares with Martin Chase, who matched it in 1997. Jones also followed that junior year with 11.0 sacks as a senior in 1995.

The most memorable single afternoon came on September 17, 1994, against Texas Tech. Jones sacked the quarterback five times in that game, which is the Oklahoma single-game record, and the same record book credits him with six tackles for loss that day.

His senior year brought All-American recognition in 1995. The New York Giants then selected him with the fifth overall pick in the 1996 NFL Draft. For Sooner fans trading sack-leader trivia, his career total remains the figure to beat, and the record-book list is worth checking again after each new season.
